notes: Three things a mechanic asked for. The method of compliance is now a picker: 25 wordings in six groups, with the serial number, the date and the airframe hours filled in from the aeroplane in front of you, and a "keep this wording" button that puts a shop's own phrasing at the top of the list on every job after. Every not-applicable line carries its reason, because "N/A" on its own is what shops get written up for. The search now covers the airframe and every component on the list — starter, alternator, fuel pump, transponder, ELT — not four named accessory slots. And the logbook entry names them, grouped, so a reader can see the airframe was assessed rather than left out.
validated_against: The FAA's own model search on drs.faa.gov, 23 models, Status=Current: 693 directives listed, 693 returned, 0 wrongly set aside. Perfect on every individual model. AD Toolbox's airframe lists hold 528 of the same 693 — mostly by design, since their appliance directives sit in a separate unmatched list of 581.
reliability: 40 aircraft configurations searched end to end: 0 page errors, 0 problems. 167 self checks passing. Full entries to read across the 40 fell from 3,847 to 2,036, with 1,811 kept as one-line rows.

index.source: FAA Dynamic Regulatory System, AD Final Rules

fix: The links were the bug behind "several of the links are broken or don't return anything". They were SEARCHES, not documents: post-1994 a Federal Register search for the AD number, everything older the DRS browse page — the unfiltered list of all 17,107 — because the Register's archive does not reach back that far. DRS gives every document a permanent address and the index carried the id all along. Every directive now opens its own document, 1940s included.
storage: The directive index no longer shares a database with jobs and photographs. It lives in Cache Storage under 'adx-1'. Any copy left in the old place is deleted on first load. This is the second half of the 30 August fix: the database that wedged that morning is now smaller and is never touched by an AD search.
